propositions: Per-test Git subprocesses in the _no_repo_commits guard cause ~207 runner-seconds (~75s wall-time on macOS three-worker) overhead across the full 13,255-test suite, averaging 7.826ms per rev-parse HEAD probe.
The guard must preserve exact per-test HEAD-move detection, test attribution, and the allow_repo_writes escape hatch while eliminating two subprocess calls per test.
An in-process HEAD fingerprint approach requires handling symbolic loose refs, packed refs, detached HEAD, and linked worktrees without a consensus-backed safe primitive for all Git storage formats.

OSS consensus (pytest, pip, Poetry, pre-commit 4/4) rejects per-test source-checkout Git subprocesses, but neither adding a Git library, hand-parsing all ref formats, nor removing the checkout-attribution guard meets the fidelity and approval bar.
The session dirty-tree backstop and existing repo-isolation tests must remain enabled and unweakened.
No implementation was automatically approved; the ticket was closed as wontfix by operator disposition after blocking pending explicit design choice or new evidence for a safe primitive.
